doc.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Hearing his first album and Floyd Levin's review
summary: Rowe plays a track from Kellso's first released album, and they discuss a review noting Bix, Butterfield and Davison echoes, and critics generally.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Well I wanted to play something here, and see if you recognize it.
That’s a good question, because there’s two cornet players on that album. It could be a little confusing. That’s the first released album that I’m on.

Well, you’re probably familiar with what they said about you, but I wanted to get your opinion on it, regarding this particular tune, it says “Kellso tips his horn just a bit in Bix Beiderbecke’s direction. There are also occasional nods towards Billy Butterfield’s lyrical constructions and Wild Bill Davison’s ruminating low notes.” Did you know you were doing all that?
Well it wasn’t entirely conscious, but I’d have to say I’m honored that he said those nice things. I think those are certainly some of the people that influenced me a lot and
especially when playing this kind of music in that kind of setting. So he was on the ball. Who was that? Was that Floyd Levin?
I’m glad to hear you say that because sometimes you — Floyd Levin, yeah.
Yeah, he’s a good writer, good guy.
Sometimes you wonder, when you read things that the critics or record reviewers write, if the musicians really agree with it you know.

Yeah, sometimes they’re right on and they see things as musicians do or close to it, or they describe things in a very good way, which is a hard thing to do, describing music with words has always been a challenging thing. So I have to give these guys some credit and give them a little leeway. But there’s times when they come up with stuff and it’s like, is he listening to the same thing that I’m listening to? Or they read a lot into things sometimes. But he’s one of the good ones, and I’m honored that he’d say those things about me.
